title: Staff login with a one-time code

sections.background: Store staff share one password per store. When someone leaves, the password is changed by hand in every till. A personal login with a one-time code removes the shared password.
sections.requirements:
1. A staff member signs in with a staff number and a six-digit code sent to the store tablet.
2. A code expires after five minutes and works once.
3. Five wrong codes lock the staff number for fifteen minutes.
4. A manager can disable a staff number at once.
sections.design: The till asks the auth service for a code; the service stores a hash of the code with its expiry and sends the code to the store tablet. The till then exchanges the staff number and the code for a session token.
sections.data-and-tables:
| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `staff_no` | six digits, unique per store |
| `code_hash` | SHA-256 of the code, never the code |
| `expires_at` | five minutes after the code was made |
sections.scope:
**In scope:** login, lockout, manager disable.

**Not in scope:** fingerprint login, head office accounts.
sections.test-plan:
- Unit tests for expiry, single use and lockout.
- An end-to-end test on a test till and tablet.
- A manual check in one pilot store.
sections.risks:
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Tablet offline, no code arrives | fall back to the manager override for one hour |
| Codes guessed | lockout after five attempts |
sections.rollout: Pilot in two stores behind a flag for two weeks, then one region a week. Roll back by turning the flag off; the shared password stays valid until the last region moves.
